Industry insurance

Insurance for Airbnb and Short-Stay Hosts in Kenya

Short-stay accommodation is not always the same risk as an owner-occupied home. Frequent guests, furnished units, cleaning staff, shared facilities and platform bookings can affect how insurers view the property. Hosts should disclose how the premises are used and confirm that the policy responds to short-stay activity.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

Risks to consider

Property and contents

Furniture, appliances, décor and guest-use items may be exposed to accidental damage, fire, theft and other insured events.

Guest liability

Guests or visitors may allege injury or property damage during their stay.

Use of the property

Short-stay or commercial use may not be treated the same as ordinary residential occupancy under every policy.

Revenue interruption

An insured event may prevent bookings while repairs or reinstatement take place.

Staff and service providers

Cleaning, maintenance and other support activities create additional exposures.

Insurance covers to discuss

  • Home or property insurance suitable for the declared use
  • Contents and furnishings
  • Public liability
  • Business interruption or loss of rental income where available
  • WIBA for eligible employees
  • Equipment cover where relevant

What to have ready

  • Property ownership or lease details
  • Location and construction details
  • Number of units and beds
  • Guest occupancy and booking pattern
  • Furniture, appliances and contents value
  • Cleaning and maintenance arrangements
  • Security and fire protection
  • Current policy and claims history

The appropriate cover depends on your activities, policy terms, insurer underwriting and availability. This page is general information, not a guarantee that any particular risk is covered.
